task: Implement dedicated staff/admin login plus TOTP enrollment and challenge UX using the canonical workforce assurance primitives without enabling global AAL2 authorization enforcement.

exceptions.reason: Intentional preview-only pilot access consumer. Stage 1 workforce MFA UX explicitly excludes Builder/template/pilot acceptance work; changing this route would expand the development transaction beyond the accepted block.

Intentional template-preview authentication consumer. Its return target includes storefront-template-preview rather than the admin-only workforce return contract, and Builder/template behavior is explicit non-scope for this block.

Intentional regression evidence for the unchanged template-preview login contract; it must remain aligned with src/lib/auth/template-preview-access.ts while Builder/template work stays outside this transaction.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The flow handles workforce credentials, Supabase MFA factor enrollment and privileged-session assurance. It must compose the existing identity authority, preserve customer authentication boundaries, fail closed on missing MFA/context evidence and avoid prematurely changing global admin authorization enforcement.

acceptanceCriteria: A dedicated staff/admin login route authenticates workforce users without modifying shopper registration or customer MFA policy.
When the canonical workforce policy requires a factor and none is verified, the UI starts Supabase TOTP enrollment and displays both QR data and the manual secret fallback.
When verified TOTP factors exist but the current session is below AAL2, the UI challenges a verified factor and only continues after Supabase verification succeeds.
A platform owner is guided until two verified TOTP factors exist and the current session is AAL2.
Successful completion returns to the originally requested safe admin target, while invalid or external return targets fall back to /admin.
MFA/context loading errors and interrupted enrollment fail closed inside the workforce flow; abandoned unverified enrollment can be cancelled and unenrolled.
The UI remains usable on narrow mobile and desktop widths without localStorage/sessionStorage MFA state or OTP-secret persistence.
This block does not add requireAdmin, middleware or API-wide AAL2 authorization enforcement.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the sole TOTP secret, factor verification and AAL authority.
The existing workforce assurance policy remains the sole source of required factor count.
Customer AuthForm behavior and customer MFA policy remain unchanged.
A client-side success state never substitutes for server-owned workforce role context.
No workforce flow writes OTP secrets, challenge codes or MFA readiness to localStorage or sessionStorage.
Admin authorization enforcement remains unchanged until the next dedicated high-risk auth block.

failureModes: A shopper credential is accepted by the workforce surface and accidentally treated as staff authority.
A platform owner verifies one factor and is redirected before the required second verified factor exists.
An unverified enrollment is abandoned and repeatedly accumulates stale factors that obstruct later enrollment.
MFA snapshot or role-context retrieval fails and the UI continues as though no MFA were required.
A crafted next parameter redirects a privileged login to an external or non-admin target.
The workforce UX starts enforcing AAL2 globally and blocks low-risk staff beyond the accepted policy.
Mobile layout hides the QR fallback, code field or recovery controls required to finish enrollment.
edgeCases: Platform owner with zero verified factors at AAL1 enrolls factor one, verifies it, then is guided to enroll factor two.
Platform owner with one verified factor at AAL1 first challenges that factor, then enrolls and verifies the second factor.
Platform owner with two verified factors at AAL1 challenges one verified factor and then proceeds.
Merchant admin with one verified factor at AAL1 challenges and proceeds after AAL2.
Low-risk platform operator or store staff with zero required factors proceeds without forced enrollment.
Customer-only user signing in on the workforce route receives a staff-access error and is not granted admin navigation.
An interrupted unverified enrollment can be cancelled and removed before a fresh enrollment starts.

alternatives.summary: Expose the dedicated workforce login as an auth-owned Next.js page under /api/auth/workforce-login, consuming server-resolved role context and the existing MFA primitives.
alternatives.reason: This keeps the substantive high-risk release unit entirely inside auth-access-authority. The existing admin-entry redirect bridge is deliberately deferred to a separate lower-risk stacked release unit rather than mixing customer-account routing into the auth PR.

alternatives.summary: Add staff role detection and MFA screens directly inside the existing shopper AuthForm.
alternatives.reason: It would mix customer and workforce intent, increase route/policy coupling and risk turning a shared customer presentation component into a second workforce authority.

alternatives.summary: Wire AAL2 checks into middleware and requireAdmin at the same time as the first MFA UX.
alternatives.reason: The Product Owner explicitly separated UX proof from the next high-risk enforcement block; combining them would expand blast radius before enrollment and recovery behavior is proven.

specialistReviews.finding: The workforce surface must compose the canonical identity primitives and may not duplicate required-factor logic or factor persistence in presentation code.
specialistReviews.resolution: Server role context returns only the role-derived requirement, while enrollment/challenge calls remain wrappers over the existing workforce MFA client and Supabase Auth.

specialistReviews.finding: A successful password sign-in is only AAL1 and cannot be treated as privileged-ready; provider/context errors and unsafe return targets must not create a bypass.
specialistReviews.resolution: The workforce flow fails closed on context/MFA errors, requires the canonical next MFA step before redirect, and normalizes return intent to a local /admin target.

specialistReviews.finding: Enrollment must remain operable without QR scanning and on narrow screens, including explicit cancellation of an in-progress factor.
specialistReviews.resolution: The planned surface exposes the TOTP secret fallback, touch-sized controls, responsive single-column layout and an enrollment cancellation path that unenrolls the unverified factor.

challenge.scenario: A platform owner has one verified factor but the password login session is AAL1.
challenge.finding: Enrolling factor two immediately would skip proof that the current session controls the already verified factor.
challenge.resolution: The state machine follows the canonical policy: challenge the existing verified factor first, then enroll the missing second factor.

challenge.scenario: A user closes or cancels the screen after Supabase creates an unverified TOTP enrollment.
challenge.finding: Leaving stale unverified factors can accumulate and make later enrollment ambiguous.
challenge.resolution: Cancellation explicitly unenrolls the in-progress factor, and a new enrollment cleans stale unverified TOTP factors before creating another.

challenge.scenario: The role-context endpoint or Supabase MFA snapshot fails after password authentication.
challenge.finding: Treating the failure as zero required factors would turn an availability error into an authentication downgrade.
challenge.resolution: The workforce UI enters an error/retry state and never redirects to the requested admin target until context and MFA evidence load successfully.

challenge.scenario: A normal shopper reaches /fiokom without an admin login intent.
challenge.finding: A broad redirect to the workforce page would silently change the customer login contract.
challenge.resolution: Only the existing reason=login intent with a normalized /admin next target bridges to the dedicated workforce route; all ordinary customer account behavior remains untouched.

challenge.scenario: An attacker supplies next=//evil.example or another non-admin local path.
challenge.finding: Returning blindly after MFA could create an open redirect or cross-surface privileged-login confusion.
challenge.resolution: The page normalizes the value with the existing safe local return helper and accepts only /admin targets, otherwise falling back to /admin.

challenge.scenario: A low-risk staff role has no verified factor and no sensitive-boundary requirement.
challenge.finding: Forcing enrollment merely because the user entered the staff portal would contradict the accepted workforce MFA policy.
challenge.resolution: The server derives requiredFactors from the canonical policy; zero-factor roles proceed without a synthetic MFA requirement.

challenge.scenario: A customer-only account successfully authenticates with email and password on the workforce route.
challenge.finding: Authentication alone does not prove workforce authorization.
challenge.resolution: A server-owned workforce-context lookup must resolve platform or store staff role authority before any MFA decision or admin redirect occurs.

challenge.scenario: The workforce context API directly imports tenant instance and store-role authority from an Identity-domain route.
challenge.finding: Codebase Atlas rejects the direct DOMAIN-IDENTITY to DOMAIN-TENANCY dependency because only the canonical auth boundary modules are authorized to consume tenancy context.
challenge.resolution: Resolve platform/store workforce context inside src/lib/auth/admin-api.ts, whose Identity-to-Tenancy boundary is already an explicit architecture contract, and keep the route as a thin Identity API consumer.

challenge.scenario: Reference Sync finds legacy /fiokom login literals in pilot and template-preview paths after requireAdmin moves ordinary admin login to the dedicated workforce route.
challenge.finding: Blindly rewriting those consumers would cross the PO non-scope boundary into Builder/template and preview acceptance behavior, including a non-admin storefront-template-preview return contract.
challenge.resolution: Keep the three consumers unchanged and record exact fingerprint-scoped review exceptions; no broad exception or route rewrite is allowed.

challenge.scenario: The first complete workforce UX diff spans auth-access-authority, customer-account and storefront-ui, causing the production Release Risk Budget to block a high-risk auth change mixed with lower-risk subsystems.
challenge.finding: Keeping the convenient /fiokom bridge and a generic app page would violate the canonical rule that a high-risk subsystem must be the only substantive production release subsystem.
challenge.resolution: Revert customer-account and middleware changes and keep the workforce page under src/app/api/auth ownership. The existing middleware remains read-only; a separate stacked customer-account release unit will bridge its existing /fiokom?reason=login&next=/admin intent to the verified workforce route.

proofPlan: Run deterministic regression tests covering safe workforce return routing, customer-auth isolation, Supabase-only MFA usage, platform-owner second-factor progression and abandoned enrollment cleanup.
Run the full quality test suite so existing customer account, platform portal, RBAC, navigation and Known Failure regressions remain green.
Run TypeScript validation for the new App Router page, route handler and client MFA state machine.
Run production build proof to catch Server/Client Component boundary, Next.js routing and responsive JSX compilation failures.
Use exact-head CI Completion Truth evidence before closure; do not treat an automatically created Vercel preview or Vercel READY status as completion proof.

requirements.requirement: The dedicated workforce login provides safe staff/admin password authentication, canonical Supabase TOTP enrollment/challenge UX, two-factor platform-owner progression, safe admin return routing and fail-closed error/cancellation behavior without changing customer MFA policy or global AAL2 authorization enforcement.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No custom OTP verification service, secret persistence or browser storage may become an MFA authority.
Ordinary shopper login/registration and customer MFA policy must remain unchanged by the workforce flow.
This block must not add middleware/API-wide or requireAdmin AAL2 authorization enforcement.

notes: Stage 1 MR1-WORKFORCE-IDENTITY UI block only. The canonical AAL2/TOTP primitives from PR #848 are consumed, not reimplemented. The next separate high-risk auth block will add authorization enforcement after this UX is exact-head VERIFIED. CI attempt 1 exposed an Authority Graph dependency drift in the new route; scope was widened to the existing canonical admin-api identity boundary rather than adding a new cross-domain exception. Reference Sync review confirmed three preview/template consumers are intentionally unchanged and are acknowledged only through exact finding fingerprints. Release Risk Budget required high-risk isolation, so the final transaction removes customer-account/storefront substantive edits and keeps the workforce UX entirely inside auth-access-authority; /staff/login is a middleware alias only. Atlas also proves src/middleware.ts has no canonical domain classification; middleware therefore remains read-only in this auth release unit. The normal admin-entry bridge will be a separate stacked customer-account transaction after the auth unit is verified.
